subject.title: The Skill Accumulation Problem: How many skills before your agent gets confused?

question: Should ClawHub own a skill-accumulation governance contract, and if so should the first scope be task-context recommendation, conflict/load-policy metadata, or documentation around existing pinning and layering practices?
rationale: The remaining gap is not a localized source bug; it changes publisher metadata, registry semantics, privacy boundaries, and possibly OpenClaw runtime loading behavior.

options.title: Define RFC First
options.body: Write the product/spec contract for recommender inputs, conflict semantics, privacy, and runtime enforcement before implementation.

options.title: Narrow To Metadata
options.body: Add only manifest conflict/dependency/load-policy fields now, accepting that it may not solve session-context recommendation or runtime priority behavior.

options.title: Document Practices Only
options.body: Keep ClawHub as discovery plus pinning and publish guidance for pruning, layering, and production locks without adding new registry behavior yet.

recommendation.title: Define RFC First
recommendation.body: Write the product/spec contract for recommender inputs, conflict semantics, privacy, and runtime enforcement before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision crosses CODEOWNERS-listed schema, Convex skills, HTTP API, and CLI schema surfaces.
